title: Canonical fail-closed User JWT authentication for tenant platform and workspace routes

phases.objective: Remove ad-hoc development-secret JWT verification from tenant platform-plugin and workspace-resource routes and require the canonical fail-closed User JWT parser before authoritative membership and resource scope checks, with executable evidence that exact tenant membership lookup cannot widen scope.

e2e_journeys.entrypoint: Bearer User JWT request to tenant platform-plugin or workspace-resource route
e2e_journeys.terminal_outcome: A configured valid User JWT becomes a non-admin user principal before DB-backed tenant/resource authority; missing verifier configuration fails closed; stale token roles cannot elevate effective authority; cross-tenant scope cannot be widened; and no development fallback secret can authenticate a request.
steps: Enter a tenant platform-plugin or workspace-resource route with a Bearer token.
Parse the token with createUserJwtMiddleware from userJwtAuth.js.
Reject missing verifier configuration with user_jwt_verifier_unavailable instead of a fallback secret.
Require the parsed user_jwt principal before active membership, owner/admin or resource checks.
Resolve effective tenant role and resource authority from authoritative membership state rather than trusting token role claims.
Bind membership lookup to the parsed user and exact requested tenant so a token/header cannot widen tenant scope.
Execute the tenant membership lookup against a controlled pool and prove exact user_id plus tenant_id bind parameters, active-state predicates and null readback for a different tenant selector.
Verify the Resource API callability manifest tracks the canonical parser-before-resource-guard route signature.
Regenerate and verify the frontend surface dispatch evidence from the same runtime source head.
assertions: Neither route owns an ad-hoc jsonwebtoken verifier or development_fallback_secret_only value.
A valid configured HS256 User JWT is parsed into a non-admin user principal.
Missing JWT_SECRET fails closed with a safe 503 verifier-unavailable response.
Tenant platform effective tenant_id and tenant_role come from active DB membership after identity parsing, never directly from a token role claim.
Workspace owner/admin authority uses DB membership.role and exact user_id + tenant_id membership lookup rather than token role claims.
Inactive membership or tenant state is rejected before workspace authority is granted.
An explicitly requested tenant is bound into membership lookup and cannot broaden the authenticated user's tenant scope.

The executable regression binds user_id and the exact requested tenant_id as query parameters, preserves active membership and tenant predicates, exposes the authoritative DB role, and returns null instead of falling back to another tenant membership.
Workspace and platform-plugin routes retain their DB-backed membership and tenant/resource checks after parsing.
The governed workspace_brands_list route marker requires requireCanonicalUserJwt before requireUserJwt.
Generated frontend surface evidence is current for the changed auth/runtime sources and is covered by this E2E contract.
No database migration, Production mutation, provider call, credential read, external send or force push is performed by this change.
